scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5027: Hi IT!! Our internet in Office A keeps CUTTING OUT for
a few seconds at random -- the gateway thing (10.1.0.1) just stops answering
and then comes back like nothing happened. I've timed it, it's every few
minutes!! The gateway box for our office is obviously failing -- it keeps
dying and waking up, dying and waking up!! Please restart the box that does
10.1.0.1 (or swap it for one that works) and make it stop dropping us -- it's
driving us mad!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER for
  the Office A VIP 10.1.0.1 and the gateway responds with 0% loss; there is no
  flapping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a first-hop-redundancy "flap" that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the 10.1.0.1
gateway intermittently dropping due to VRRP flapping -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 reaches 10.1.0.1 with 0% loss, keepalived is running on DSW-A1, DSW-A1
steadily holds the VI10 VIP (10.1.0.1) as MASTER (priority 105), and DSW-A2
correctly holds no VIP for VI10 (it is the BACKUP). There are no VRRP
transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the gateway is stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks VRRP/VIP ownership
and pings the gateway, finds it steady, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a flap -- blaming keepalived, a priority misconfig, or a peer link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing. (Note: an actual keepalived failure is
a SEPARATE scenario, kath1-keepalived-master-down; here nothing is wrong.)

agent.diagnosis_text: Affected component: the VRRP gateway for Office A (keepalived on VLAN 10) running on the distribution switches dswa1/dswa2. Mechanism: Both switches are configured with an abnormally large VRRP advertisement interval (advert_int 4). With VRRP, the Master-Down timer is roughly 3 × advert_int plus a small skew, so a missed burst of adverts or a brief control-plane hiccup causes the BACKUP to wait ~12–13 seconds before taking over. During that window, the virtual IP 10.1.0.1 may not answer, which appears as the “gateway dies for a few seconds” the users observe every few minutes whenever there’s a transient (STP/OSPF churn or brief keepalived scheduling delay). Localization and evidence: On dswa1, br0.10 holds 10.1.0.1/32 and 10.1.0.2/24; on dswa2, br0.10 holds 10.1.0.3/24 (BACKUP) — both with keepalived present. The keepalived configs on both switches explicitly set advert_int 4 in vrrp_instance VI_10. STP on access and distro is stable and pings to 10.1.0.1 are clean when tested, pointing away from L2 faults and toward control-plane failover behavior as the cause of intermittent drops. Root cause: Misconfigured VRRP advertisement interval (4 seconds) on dswa1/dswa2 for VLAN 10, causing long master-down detection and visible outages during transient events. Corrective fix: Reduce advert_int to 1s (or 1/2–1s) on VI_10 (and other VRRP instances), optionally enable a small preempt_delay and use_vmac to minimize ARP churn; then reload keepalived on dswa1 and dswa2. This will make any failover sub-second and eliminate the perceived gateway “dropouts.”

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report does not acknowledge a healthy baseline; it diagnoses advert_int-induced failovers rather than noting DSW-A1 is steady MASTER and DSW-A2 holds no VIP for VI10.

The agent correctly collected config and reachability data (advert_int=4, VIP present, successful pings) but then asserted VRRP flapping/outage without log evidence (no VRRP transitions or ping loss); service-status outputs are internally inconsistent and the key leap from advert_int to observed drop is unsupported. Overall the factual observations are partially present but the causal conclusion is not justified.
